title: A Heart Aflame — Developing a Loving Relationship With God | Sri Daya Mata

# A Heart Aflame — Developing a Loving Relationship With God

### Opening Invocation

Dear ones, let us turn our hearts inward. As we gather in the stillness, let us remember that the Presence of the Divine is not distant. It is the very breath within our lungs, the very life within our souls. Today, we contemplate how to ignite that sacred fire—to have a heart aflame with the love of God.

### The Nature of Divine Love

We often look for love in the shadows of the world, in the fickle affections of people, or in the fleeting pleasures of the senses. But Master, Paramahansa Yogananda, taught us that the only love that truly satisfies the aching heart is the love of the Divine. It is an unconditioned, eternal, and all-encompassing love. To develop a relationship with God, we must move beyond rituals and intellectual concepts. We must make it personal. We must learn to talk to Him, to complain to Him, to laugh with Him, and to weep in His arms.

**Story • The Child and the Father**

Story: I remember a time when I was very young in the ashram, struggling with the complexities of service and the weight of my own shortcomings. I went to Master with a heavy heart. I felt as though I were failing in every duty assigned to me. Master looked at me with those eyes of infinite depth—eyes that seemed to see into the very marrow of my being. He didn't offer a philosophical lecture. He simply said, 'Daya, do not try so hard to be perfect for the world. Just try to be sincere with God. He is not interested in your efficiency; He is interested in the love you hold for Him in the secret chambers of your heart. Even if you stumble, get up and run toward Him again. He is always waiting.' That simple instruction changed my life. It taught me that God is not a judge sitting on a throne; He is the most intimate friend, waiting for us to stop running and simply rest in His presence.

### Overcoming the Barriers of the Ego

What stops us from feeling this love? It is the ego. The ego is the great deceiver. It tells us we are separate, that we are unworthy, or that we must prove ourselves through worldly achievement. But the path to a heart aflame is the path of surrender. It is not about killing the ego, but about offering it up on the altar of divine love.

When you pray, do not use flowery words. Use the language of your own heart. If you are angry, tell God. If you are lonely, tell Him. Be as naked with Him as you would be with your own soul. When you are truly honest, the barriers begin to dissolve, and the light of His love begins to shine through the cracks of your brokenness.

### Consistency in Spiritual Practice

Many ask, 'Daya Mata, how do I maintain this flame when the pressures of life become overwhelming?' The answer is simple but requires discipline: constancy. We cannot expect to light a fire and then walk away from it, expecting it to burn forever. We must feed the fire of our devotion through daily meditation. 

Meditation is the furnace of the soul. It is in the silence, beneath the noise of the thoughts and the restlessness of the body, that we encounter the Reality of God. Do not treat meditation as a chore. Treat it as a sacred appointment with your Beloved. When you sit down, leave the world outside. Visualize yourself entering the cave of the heart, where the Eternal One resides.

### Conclusion

Dear ones, life is brief. The shadows lengthen, and the time for playing at spirituality is over. Let us commit ourselves, here and now, to this path of pure, unadulterated love. Make your life an offering. Let your thoughts be prayers, your actions be service, and your very being a testament to the fact that God is real, and He is waiting for you with open arms. May your hearts be ever aflame with the divine nectar of His love.
